title: Non-negative differential mobility of one-dimensional underdamped Langevin dynamics: Proof via mapping to a marginally stable oscillator
abstract: For an underdamped particle driven by a constant non-conservative force across a periodic potential in one spatial dimension at finite temperature, numerical studies have shown that the differential mobility is non-negative. Here, an analytical proof will be given that is based on expressing the differential mobility by the long-time mean position of a marginally stable harmonic oscillator subject to noise in its stiffness.
summary: This paper provides a rigorous analytical proof that the differential mobility for an underdamped particle in a periodic potential is non-negative. It achieves this by transforming the stochastic dynamics into an analysis of a marginally stable harmonic oscillator. The result is significant for understanding transport properties in systems driven by external forces.
main_problem: To provide an analytical proof that the differential mobility ($\mu_d$) of one-dimensional underdamped Langevin dynamics driven by a constant non-conservative force across a periodic potential is non-negative.
main_result: The differential mobility $\mu_d$ is proven to be non-negative ($\mu_d \ge 0$) for the underdamped case, with specific results derived for the zero-potential and binding potential limits.
method: The proof maps the problem to the long-time behavior of a marginally stable harmonic oscillator, utilizing projection operators and solving coupled equations of motion derived from the Fokker-Planck equation.
model_or_system: The system is a one-dimensional particle undergoing underdamped Langevin dynamics in a periodic potential $V(x)$, governed by the equation $m\ddot{x} + \gamma \dot{x} = f -V'(x) + \xi$.
key_observables: Differential mobility ($\mu_d$), mean velocity ($\overline{v}(f)$), and the time evolution of the difference between velocity and mean velocity.
important_parameters: The driving force $f$, the damping coefficient $\gamma$, and the potential curvature $V''(x)$.
main_assumptions: Assumes the existence of a unique stationary distribution and exponential convergence to it.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the definition of $\mu_d$, relates it to the dynamics of a linearized oscillator, and then uses projection operators and Laplace transforms to derive and analyze the long-time limit of the mean correlation functions, leading to the final non-negativity proof.
why_interesting: The mathematical techniques used—analyzing long-time limits of stochastic differential equations via projection operators and spectral analysis—are highly relevant to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics and open quantum systems.
